Area.evidence_source: Suicides in prison are an ongoing cause for concern and were identified as a priority for action in 'Preventing suicide in England: a cross-government outcomes strategy to save lives' (Department of Health 2012). The challenge of understanding and preventing suicides among offenders outside prison has received limited attention, despite the age-adjusted risk of suicide for male offenders leaving prison being eight times the national average (Pratt et al. 2006), and over a quarter of all such deaths occur within the first 4 weeks of release. Sattar (2001) found that 22.3% of all deaths in individuals under Probation Service supervision were being catalogued as suicides, often by violent means. Revolvers or churners; those frequently in and out of the prison system, appear to pose a particularly high level of risk to themselves. Revolving between chaotic lives in the community and repeated short spells of incarceration, they are often not under supervision of probation services on release and generally have little contact with primary care or specialist mental health services (Howerton et al. 2007, Williamson 2006), contributing to their high risk of suicide.
